observations:
LM2 Torah 113 is a single-sentence moral aphorism — one of the shortest entries in Likutay Moharan Tinyana. The full text reads: 'One in whom the Divine name merely flickers (מִי שֶׁרַק מִתְנוֹצֵץ לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ) — when he does, God forbid, even one thing that is not as it should be in its perfection (meaning: even if there is no trace of sin in it, God forbid, and no complete physical desire in physicality, only that he does not do the thing with the utmost perfection of holiness as it truly should be) — it is fitting that his soul should completely expire from the sheer intensity of regret (חֲרָטָה) and shame (בּוּשָׁה).'

The teaching contains no bechina language (no 'X הוא בחינת Y', no 'X נקרא Y', no 'X כנ"ל' equating concepts, no parallelism declaring two things to share the same essential nature). The only relationships present are causal/eitza: (1) a person close to God who acts without absolute perfection → (2) his soul should expire from regret and shame. This is moral exhortation about the spiritual standard expected of those at the highest level of closeness to God.

The concepts in the text — מִתְנוֹצֵץ לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ (one in whom God's name flickers), שְׁלֵמוּת הַקְּדֻשָּׁה (perfection of holiness), חֲרָטָה (regret), and בּוּשָׁה (shame) — appear in the text but without any bechina equivalence between them. A new package requires 3+ concepts connected by explicit bechina language forming an independent domain; that condition is not met here.

Conclusion: NO_NEW_PACKAGES. Reference 1113 has zero bechina entries in the dataset, and the source text contains no bechina constructions that would warrant adding any.
